title: Whether to install a dual-proof cathedral reality spine
problem: The master cathedral source expands the persistent destination, but the repository still reports VDM=0, CVO=0, HARDENED=0 and unresolved runtime ownership. The decision is whether to copy the source into a monolithic runtime prompt, defer it entirely, or preserve it through classified intent, one canonical capability crosswalk, and distinct internal and external proof gates.
baseline: PR #87 proposes a durable InstitutionalRuntime but reports no clean verified external outcome; PR #88 adds inert organizational contracts and a falsification plan while protecting static DurableWorkflow and retaining VDM=0. The canonical capability registry remains blueprint/registry.py.

alternatives.name: Monolithic cathedral prompt
alternatives.description: Inject the entire founder architecture into every model call and treat it as the operational control plane.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Only as a source archive or unusually justified long-context input, never as a replacement for machine policy and proof.

alternatives.name: Documentation-only preservation
alternatives.description: Store the master architecture and take no machine-checkable action.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Suitable only if the repository cannot safely accept additive governance artifacts.

alternatives.name: Single proof gate
alternatives.description: Use one success label for internal execution and external outcomes.
disadvantages: Internal success can masquerade as market or settlement truth
External effects can skip restart proof
alternatives.revival_evidence: None while internal durability and external consequence remain materially different risk domains.

alternatives.name: Dual-proof additive spine
alternatives.description: Classify the source, map it to canonical owners, and require VDM before separately authorized CVO while leaving runtime and live execution untouched.
disadvantages: Cannot itself close VDM or CVO
alternatives.revival_evidence: This is the selected design and remains valid while it blocks overclaiming without duplicating runtime semantics.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: Leave the master source in the conversation and keep existing code unchanged; no new duplication occurs, but source coverage, proof semantics, and authority scope remain implicit.
disadvantages: VDM and CVO can be conflated

roles.position: Preserve all 31 cathedral sections as classified destinations and make explicit that source text does not create executable authority.
Add policy and crosswalk artifacts only; reuse blueprint/registry.py and defer runtime implementation until PR #70/#87 ownership is decided.
Dual-gate vocabulary can become new theater unless current counters remain zero and substitutes are explicitly forbidden.
Accept a small additive package with standard-library tests, explicit rollback, no runtime code, and no edit to the completed PR #88 deliberation.
Require independent evidence roots, lawful operators, consent and anti-manipulation controls before CVO; VDM must remain consequence-free.

evidence.claim: The repository has a canonical evidence-backed capability registry.
evidence.finding: The registry already separates awarded rung, current reality, gaps, owners, and evidence; a new registry would be duplication.

evidence.claim: A durable runtime line exists as a proposal but whole-body closure is not proven.
evidence.finding: InstitutionalRuntime and restart recovery are proposed while CVO=0, HARDENED=0 and whole-body closure remains false.

evidence.claim: Organizational Morphogenesis Phase 1 is inert and keeps static DurableWorkflow as the protected baseline.
evidence.finding: Three schemas and tests exist; no runtime code or VDM is added.

counterevidence.claim: A new evidence policy can increase documents without increasing capability.
counterevidence.reference: Master source anti-theater rule and current VDM=0/CVO=0
counterevidence.finding: This change must keep all proof counters at zero and be judged only as a guardrail and traceability substrate.

counterevidence.reference: uniimente-kernel PR #70, PR #87, and PR #88 ownership proposal
counterevidence.finding: No execution composition root can be added in this decision.

counterevidence.claim: Some attached pseudo-digital-life mechanisms imply self-preservation or sovereign authority.
counterevidence.finding: They remain mechanism sources only; self-sovereignty, hidden persistence, and authority creation conflict with founder-governed doctrine.

pass_1.intended_outcome: Install the smallest machine-checkable layer that preserves the complete source, distinguishes internal durability from external outcome truth, and maps every source section to an existing or explicitly missing canonical owner.

advantages.statement: Preserves the cathedral without runtime context overload.
advantages.amplified_value: All 31 sections stay retrievable while mission calls can use compiled relevant context.

advantages.statement: Separates durable mission truth from real external outcome truth.
advantages.amplified_value: Internal progress can compound without laundering sandbox success into settlement claims.

advantages.statement: Turns proof history into reusable institutional substrate.
advantages.amplified_value: Verified episodes can improve routing, topology choice, recovery, autonomy calibration, and capital allocation.
The crosswalk points to blueprint/registry.py and existing owners instead of creating a duplicate registry or runtime.
Capability promotion, merge, live graduation, and ownership decisions stay separately human-gated.

disadvantages.statement: A new evidence vocabulary can become documentation theater.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Keep VDM, CVO and HARDENED counters at zero; add tests that forbid automatic promotion and common substitutes.

disadvantages.statement: The crosswalk could become a second capability registry.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Declare blueprint/registry.py canonical in machine-readable fields and test that the crosswalk does not replace it.

disadvantages.statement: Approval language could silently ratify runtime ownership or live action.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Add a scope clarification that approves only this inert stacked change and preserves separate founder decisions.

disadvantages.statement: A single success ladder may imply CVO automatically follows VDM.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Encode distinct gate assertions, separate live graduation, and an explicit no-implication rule.

disadvantages.statement: The source manifest is a normalization rather than an exact exported transcript.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: State the boundary prominently, retain conversation provenance, and require a future exact export to be added rather than overwrite history.

comparisons.baseline: Current PR #88 head: inert OM contracts, canonical capability registry, VDM=0, CVO=0, no whole-body closure.
comparisons.do_nothing: Avoids new files but leaves the cathedral source, gate semantics, and approval scope implicit.
comparisons.simplest_viable_alternative: One prose document describing VDM and CVO; cheaper but not machine-checkable and cannot verify source-section coverage.
comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: Existing blueprint/registry.py plus PR #87 evidence language without a new policy artifact.
comparisons.reversible_experiment: Add only source, intent, policy, crosswalk, deliberation, clarification, and standard-library tests on a dedicated stacked draft PR.

rejected_alternatives.name: New cathedral runtime
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Runtime ownership is unresolved and a second composition root would fragment the Kernel.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Explicit founder selection of the canonical runtime owner and a linked Phase-2 decision.

rejected_alternatives.name: New capability-matrix service
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Only evidence that the canonical registry cannot represent the required semantics after a migration decision.

rejected_alternatives.name: Immediate Kimi swarm integration
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Provider labor is not the current bottleneck and would not close VDM or CVO.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: A sealed parallel-search benchmark showing material lift under an approved adapter charter.

pass_2.attack_summary: The design was attacked as evidence bureaucracy, source laundering, a parallel registry, an implied runtime choice, correlated self-verification, live-action authorization, provider capture, and a semantic ladder that could automatically inflate claims. The strengthened design remains an inert, additive policy layer with zero proof counters.

new_weaknesses.statement: Maintainers may update prose while forgetting machine policy or tests.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Make the JSON artifacts authoritative for checks and test all 31 section mappings, gate counters, and promotion invariants.

new_weaknesses.statement: A verifier could be named but remain economically or evidentially correlated with the builder.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Require independence from builder and operator plus a separate evidence root; correlated agents never count as independent confirmation.

new_weaknesses.statement: The proof gate could become practical authority over missions.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: The policy only constrains claims; it cannot authorize a mission, action, budget, operator, merge, or live graduation.

new_weaknesses.statement: Provider-specific swarm results could contaminate institutional continuity.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Keep provider adapters outside constitutional identity and require portable receipts and deterministic fallbacks.

new_weaknesses.statement: Later consumers may depend on the new labels before the policy is ratified.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Keep the change on a draft stacked PR; no runtime consumer or migration is included.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Policy artifacts do not create capability; counters remain zero and success is limited to traceability and fail-closed semantics.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any claim that this PR closes VDM, CVO, HARDENED, or whole-body capability.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Machine fields and tests keep blueprint/registry.py canonical.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any crosswalk consumer attempts to write capability truth independently.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: The authority clarification explicitly excludes merge, runtime selection, ownership ratification, and external action.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any later proposal requests one of the excluded actions.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: CVO requires VDM but does not follow automatically; it has separate assertions and live-graduation authority.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any promotion tooling or report infers CVO from VDM.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: The manifest is explicitly labeled as a generated normalization and cannot masquerade as verbatim source.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: An exact exported master source becomes available.

pass_2.final_design: Add a provenance-explicit source manifest, one constitutional intent, an exactly-two-pass linked decision, a noncanonical crosswalk covering all 31 sections, machine-readable dual proof policy, scope clarification, explanatory architecture note, and standard-library tests. Keep VDM=0, CVO=0, HARDENED=0; add no runtime, shared contract schema, external action, authority, merge, or ownership ratification.

residual_risks.risk: The source manifest is normalized rather than verbatim.
residual_risks.mitigation: Preserve its provenance warning and add any future exact export as a new immutable artifact with digest.

residual_risks.risk: The stacked PR depends on unresolved PR #87 and PR #88 review order.
residual_risks.mitigation: Target the PR #88 branch, keep the delta additive, and do not merge automatically.
residual_risks.review_trigger: Either base PR changes or closes.

residual_risks.risk: No real VDM or CVO is produced by this change.
residual_risks.mitigation: Keep counters zero and make runtime-owner selection plus one protected VDM the next separate decision.
residual_risks.review_trigger: Before any whole-body or external outcome claim.

dissent.handling: The Adversarial Reviewer preserves the claim that this is governance substrate, not a capability milestone. Any report counting it as gap closure must be rejected.

entries.position: Do not count this change as VDM, CVO, hardening, or whole-body progress.
entries.rationale: It adds source normalization, policy, and tests but performs no complete interrupted mission and no external state change.
entries.evidence_threshold: A separately authorized run satisfies every frozen VDM assertion under an independent verifier; CVO additionally requires a named lawful external actor and independent changed-state proof.
entries.review_trigger: Any promotion or milestone report references this change.

authority_impact.approver: Alfonso, authenticated founder instruction 'Build it' on 2026-08-29

migration_plan: No runtime or data migration. Review the stacked draft after PR #88; if retained, future capability reporting may read the dual-proof policy while blueprint/registry.py remains canonical. Runtime selection, VDM execution, live graduation, CVO, and organ migration each require later linked decisions.

steps: Close the stacked draft pull request without merge.
If merged later, revert only this source manifest, intent, policy, crosswalk, clarification, deliberation, architecture note, and tests.
Retain the reverted deliberation and reason as historical evidence.
Continue using blueprint/registry.py, the current static DurableWorkflow baseline, and existing proof claims.

kill_criteria: The crosswalk becomes a second capability registry or writes independent capability truth.
VDM, CVO, HARDENED, or whole-body closure is incremented by documentation, schema validation, tests, model output, or self-attestation.
A model, agent, swarm, organ, verifier, or proof gate creates authority.
A live external effect occurs without a named legal operator, applicable charter, reconciliation, and independent verifier.
The change selects a runtime owner, edits runtime code, or rewrites the completed PR #88 two-pass record.
An attached self-preservation or sovereign-agent mechanism is promoted into constitutional doctrine.
review_trigger: Review this stacked draft; open a new linked decision before merge if constitutional scope changes, and before runtime selection, VDM execution, live graduation, CVO, or any third strengthening pass.
